_comment: Phase 6 hosted-webapp limits/TTL/budget/concurrency. Consumed only by src/vib_agent/webapp/ -- never by pdm_core or agent/. Codes, contact email, and secrets are env vars (INVITE_CODES, CONTACT_EMAIL, RETAIN_TRACES, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), never config.
_analysis_profile_comment: Which config/thresholds.json profile the upload path analyses with. Uploads are third-party/route-collected data (CSV/XLSX/UFF/WAV/MAT), so they take 'route'. 'streaming' is the NCD sensor pipeline's frozen production profile and is NOT what an uploaded file should be scored against. Read explicitly in app.py -- never via load_thresholds()'s active_profile default, which silently pointed the whole product at 'streaming' until RUN v5 caught it.
_job_max_runtime_comment: S7. Seconds a background worker may spend on ONE job before the TTL sweep cancels it and marks it error(timeout). Measured, not chosen: a complete end-to-end job on this path is 5-6 s (eval_s7/transcripts/states_raises.json controls), so 600 s is ~100x. The clock starts when the job WINS a worker_semaphore slot (Job.worker_started_at), never at upload, so a job that merely waited behind a full queue is never killed for someone else's slowness. Deliberately NOT job_ttl_minutes: reusing the TTL would mean an analyst watches a spinner for a full hour before a hung job is called hung, which is the exact window the prototype's honest-uncertainty card was drawn for.

inference._comment: Session G schema-inference intake (.txt/.dat/.asc). Verification-gate tolerances for RECIPE-PARSED data plus the inference call's own limits. Intake tolerances, deliberately NOT in config/thresholds.json -- that file is frozen detector calibration and this is a question about whether a file was READ correctly, not about how a machine is behaving.
inference._min_bins_per_order_comment: INTAKE-HARDEN. Minimum spectral bins per shaft order for the interpreted axis to be able to resolve running speed. Catches the INFLATION half of the unit-error class (a CPM axis read as Hz), which speed_tolerance_pct cannot: an inflated axis still spans the shaft line, and _speed_presence widens its own window to 1.5x the bin step, so the coarser the misread the wider the window it accepts. Measured, not chosen -- correctly-read files across every corpus land at 6-60 bins/order (6 being a waveform's own FFT); the observed misreads were 1.0 and 0.6.
inference._max_overall_velocity_comment: INTAKE-HARDEN. Ceiling on the overall velocity an INFERRED interpretation may claim before the read is treated as a scale error rather than a machine condition. Applies only when the recipe declares a velocity unit, i.e. exactly when an ISO 20816 severity claim is at stake. Anchored to the standard: the highest boundary in config/iso_zones.json is 11.0 mm/s (group 1 flexible, C/D), so 150 is ~13x that and a genuinely disintegrating machine still gets a diagnosis. The cheapest misread observed was 940 mm/s (a dB-scaled spectrum declared as mm/s); a decimal-convention error reached 258,535. NOT detector calibration -- this is a question about whether a file was READ correctly.

_hardening_comment: RUN v6-A app-layer hardening (webapp only): per-IP sliding-window rate limits (a second layer above the per-invite-code daily caps), the free-disk floor below which new jobs get a friendly 503, and the TTL sweeper interval. Env overrides: IP_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE, IP_JOB_POSTS_PER_HOUR, DISK_MIN_FREE_MB. Not pdm_core calibration.
_speed_agreement_comment: Session E (multi-axis upload): cross-file running-speed agreement tolerance (percent). Each uploaded channel's dominant low-frequency peak must sit within this tolerance of k*shaft (k in 1..3) of the stated RPM. Assembly-layer (webapp) integrity check, NOT a pdm_core calibration constant -- it deliberately lives here and never in config/thresholds.json profiles (frozen). Max channels per upload is structurally 3 (three named form slots); max_upload_bytes is enforced PER file.
